title: The reader's place survives a loss repair beyond the P0's eight-page bound
outcome: The P0 w-1b692f268123, under its option C, restores after a loss the window that was resident before it, so the reader's place is kept for a lost range of up to eight pages. This item holds the remainder: a lost range longer than eight pages is restored only in part (nearest the tail when attached, its first eight pages when detached), and there the reader's place is still a guess. After a loss repair, a reader who was not following the tail sees the same message at the same place in the viewport whatever the length of the resident range, and a reader who was following the tail sees the newest message. To be designed after the P0 lands, when it can be seen how often the bound is reached.
acceptance: A pane-level regression with layout-backed geometry shows, for a resident range longer than eight pages, attached and detached, the reader's selected message in view at its place after each of three losses; it fails on the P0 as landed.

How often the eight-page bound is reached in use is recorded on this item before the design is chosen, and the design note says whether the answer is a larger or unbounded exact re-read, the pane reporting its place to the body owner, or leaving the bound as it is with the reason.
The exact corrected input passes the full five-stage gate and an independent Codex and Claude review with no outstanding in-scope finding of Medium or higher.
